about.title: About Siem Reap Art Center Night Market
body: The Siem Reap Art Center Night Market is an evening market space in Siem Reap, Cambodia, where locals and visitors gather after dark to browse stalls, enjoy food, and take in the town's nightlife.
Like other night markets across Cambodia and Southeast Asia, it reflects an everyday urban rhythm — a relaxed public space shaped by local commerce rather than formal tourism.
Small stalls offer handmade goods, traditional artworks, and souvenirs, while the surrounding area highlights Cambodian local arts and the casual culture of street-side evening life.

location.title: Location & How to Visit Siem Reap Art Center in Siem Reap
location.intro: Siem Reap Art Center Night Market (暹粒藝術中心夜市 / មជ្ឈមណ្ឌលសិល្បៈខេត្តសៀមរាប) sits inside Siem Reap town, Siem Reap Province, Cambodia. Use the details below to plan the trip; the interactive map is further down this page.
tips: On foot: from Pub Street or Psar Chas (Old Market), walk south toward the Siem Reap River, cross it and continue to Hospital Street (Street 17000) — roughly 10–15 minutes.
By tuk-tuk: the usual way to travel in Siem Reap; most trips from the town centre take about 5–15 minutes depending on traffic.
By car or taxi: set the destination to 'Art Center Night Market, Hospital Street' and ask to be dropped near the main entrance.

facilities.title: Visitor Services & Nearby Facilities
facilities.intro: Everything below is described by type only. This is a non-profit information page: no specific business, brand or property is recommended or endorsed, and prices and opening hours can change without notice.

cards.title: Accessibility
cards.body: The market occupies a street-level area with paved but partly uneven surfaces. Low kerbs, cables and parked motorbikes are the practical obstacles. Wheelchairs and walking frames can usually move along the main lanes; the narrower aisles and the road crossing are easier with a companion.

cards.title: Restrooms / WC
cards.body: Restrooms inside the market quarter are limited. Public facilities and the washrooms of nearby cafés, restaurants and shops are the usual option; some charge a small fee and close before the market does.

cards.title: Parking & drop-off
cards.body: There is no large dedicated car park: vehicles use the surrounding streets, where space becomes scarce from about 18:00. Tuk-tuks and ride-hailing cars normally drop passengers at the roadside entrance and wait nearby.

cards.title: Drinking water & shade
cards.body: Bottled water and cold drinks are sold throughout the market. Stall canopies and covered aisles give shade, but seating is limited. Water-refill points are becoming more common if you carry your own bottle.

cards.title: Lighting & safety
cards.body: The market lanes are lit and busy until closing time. Take extra care where the market meets the road, since motorbikes move along that edge, and keep bags in front of you in crowded aisles.

cards.title: Orientation & assistance
cards.body: The market is compact and can be walked as a loop. The plus code 9V24+W2F identifies the entrance for mapping apps, and the listed phone number is the quickest way to ask for directions during opening hours.

nearby.title: Nearby services, by type
nearby.intro: What exists in the surrounding town centre, described without naming or ranking any business.

items.title: Food & drink outlets
items.desc: Street-food stalls, casual local restaurants, coffee and juice shops cluster around the market and the riverside, most of them open into the late evening. Vegetarian, halal or allergy-specific kitchens vary from place to place and are best asked about directly.

items.title: Accommodation categories
items.desc: The town centre holds hostels, guesthouses, boutique hotels and larger hotels, several within walking distance of the market. Availability is tightest from November to February, when booking ahead is sensible.

items.title: Supermarkets & convenience stores
items.desc: Small convenience stores and daily-goods shops trade into the evening; larger supermarkets usually close earlier. Fresh produce is easiest to find in the traditional markets during the day.

items.title: ATMs, banks & currency
items.desc: ATMs and bank branches are concentrated in the centre and dispense US dollars and Cambodian riel. Cash is the norm at market stalls, small notes are the most useful, and card acceptance is limited.

items.title: Pharmacy, clinic & emergency care
items.desc: Hospital Street takes its name from the concentration of medical services in this part of town: pharmacies, clinics and hospital facilities. Opening hours differ, so call ahead outside daytime hours.

items.title: Fuel stations & EV charging
items.desc: Fuel stations are found on the main roads into town. Charging points for electric vehicles remain few, so plan a charging stop before you arrive.

items.title: Mobile data & Wi-Fi
items.desc: Local operators sell prepaid SIM and eSIM plans with good coverage in town, and most cafés and hotels provide Wi-Fi. Signal can be intermittent in the busiest market aisles.

items.title: Laundry & luggage
items.desc: Laundry services and luggage storage are common in the guesthouse quarter around the centre — useful if you leave town after an evening visit.

items.title: Bicycles, tuk-tuks & transport
items.desc: Bicycles can be rented by the day, and tuk-tuks are available on the street or through ride-hailing apps. For unmetered trips, agree the fare before departure.

items.title: Quiet space & religious sites
items.desc: Several Buddhist temples stand within walking distance. Cover shoulders and knees, remove shoes where indicated, and keep voices low when people are praying.

facilities.note: Facility descriptions reflect typical conditions on Hospital Street and in the surrounding town centre and are provided for orientation only. Services, opening hours and prices may change.

landmarks.title: Landmarks & Attractions Around Siem Reap Art Center
landmarks.intro: Siem Reap Art Center Night Market sits inside a compact, walkable part of Siem Reap town. These nearby landmarks are easy to combine with the same evening.

items.name: Psar Chas (Old Market)
items.desc: The historic central market of Siem Reap, within walking distance of the night market quarter and known for fabrics, spices and souvenirs.

items.name: Siem Reap River riverside promenade
items.desc: The riverside walkway that links the old market quarter with the northern part of town and is busiest in the early evening.

items.name: Pub Street (Street 8)
items.desc: Siem Reap's best-known evening street, next to the old market quarter and easy to reach on foot.

items.name: Wat Preah Prom Rath
items.desc: A Buddhist temple in the centre of Siem Reap town, noted for its painted walls and riverside setting.

deepDive: Cambodia's night markets are also a piece of town planning. Grouping food, crafts and evening trade into a few streets concentrates lighting, waste collection and traffic management in one place, which keeps the rest of the centre residential. The layout visitors walk through — rows of small stalls with a food section and a seating or stage area — is the practical result of that idea.

The market's position shapes its character. Hospital Street and the surrounding quarter sit between the river and the main approach roads, close enough to the guesthouse district to be reached on foot, and far enough from the temple road to serve residents as much as visitors. That is why the food rows fill up earlier than the souvenir aisles.
history.timelineTitle: Timeline of the town behind the market

timeline.title: The Angkor period
timeline.text: The temples that made this region famous are built, and with them the craft tradition — stone carving, bronze casting, weaving — that later generations of Siem Reap artisans inherit.

timeline.title: The province returns to Cambodian administration
timeline.text: Under the Franco-Siamese treaty, Siem Reap and Battambang provinces are returned to Cambodian administration, and the town begins to grow around the route to the temples.

timeline.title: The first tourist town
timeline.text: Once the temples can be reached by road, Siem Reap develops hotels and guesthouses for visitors — the beginning of the service economy that still defines the town centre.

timeline.title: Angkor becomes a World Heritage Site
timeline.text: The archaeological park is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, and international visitor numbers begin the long rise that reshapes the town's streets, markets and evening trade.

timeline.title: The evening economy grows
timeline.text: Guesthouses, restaurants and the first night markets appear in the centre. Trading shifts from a daytime market day to a second, later one that continues until midnight.

timeline.title: A walkable centre
timeline.text: The riverside and the old market quarter become the focus of evening life, with markets, food streets and craft shops clustering within a short walk of one another.

timeline.title: Art Center Night Market
timeline.text: The market trades on Hospital Street as a modern evening market: craft and souvenir rows, food stalls and a late closing time, serving residents and visitors in the same lanes.

history.craftsIntro: The goods sold in the centre are the visible end of trades that are still taught and practised across Siem Reap province.

crafts.title: Stone carving
crafts.desc: Sandstone and laterite are worked with chisels into reliefs and figures modelled on the temples. A single detailed piece can take days or weeks.

crafts.title: Silk & ikat weaving
crafts.desc: Cambodian silk is woven on handlooms, and the 'hol' technique dyes the pattern into the threads before weaving, which gives the cloth its characteristic slightly softened edges.

crafts.title: Lacquerware & woodwork
crafts.desc: Layers of lacquer are built up and polished over carved wood, often with gold or silver leaf applied in the final stages.

crafts.title: Silver & beadwork
crafts.desc: Silver has a long tradition in Cambodian jewellery, often combined with woven cord, stones or beads in designs that echo temple ornament.

history.legendsIntro: These are legends and traditions told around Siem Reap town, included as cultural background. They are not documented history of the market, and where a scientific explanation exists it is given alongside.

legends.title: Why the town is called Siem Reap
legends.body: The name is commonly explained as 'the defeat of Siam' — a folk memory of a Khmer victory over Siamese forces, said to have given the town its name. Historians treat the story as tradition rather than record, yet the name has carried that meaning for generations.

legends.title: The lake that flows both ways
legends.body: Local tradition describes the Tonle Sap as a lake that breathes. Science explains the same phenomenon: during the monsoon the swollen Mekong pushes the Tonle Sap river upstream and the lake expands several-fold; as the water level falls, the flow reverses toward the sea. Fishing, farming and the region's festivals are all organised around that reversal.

legends.title: The apsaras of Angkor
legends.body: The celestial dancers carved into the temples come from the legend of the churning of the ocean, when gods and demons stirred the sea and the apsaras rose from the water. Their poses are the ancestor of Cambodian classical dance, which can still be seen performed in town.

legends.title: The two guardian statues
legends.body: Siem Reap town keeps a well-known shrine with two revered Buddha images, understood locally as brother and sister, who are asked for protection and good fortune. It is a working place of worship, so visitors dress and behave accordingly.

legends.title: The water festival
legends.body: When the lake finally drains, the town celebrates with boat races, illuminated floats and fireworks. The festival marks the turn of the water year, and the strings of lights over an evening market carry the same idea in a smaller, everyday form.

paragraphs: Siem Reap Art Center Night Market belongs to the modern chapter of the town's history. Siem Reap grew into an international destination around the Angkor archaeological park, and an evening market economy grew alongside it to serve both residents and the visitors who arrive each season.

Cambodian night markets are, above all, working commercial spaces. They are usually laid out as rows of small, individually owned stalls and they follow the rhythm of the day: setting up in the late afternoon, filling up after dark, and closing late in the evening.

For Siem Reap, the Art Center Night Market matters because it keeps handicraft and food trade in the centre of town. Buyers and makers meet directly at the stall, which is why these markets remain a practical point of contact with Cambodian craft traditions and everyday cooking.
This page describes the market as it is publicly listed. It makes no claim of official status and reproduces no promotional material; stalls, opening hours and services may change over time.

transport.title: How To Get There
transport.intro: The market sits within Siem Reap town, within reach of most central areas. Below are practical ways to reach it.

airport.title: From Siem Reap International Airport
airport.desc: The airport is located outside the town (about 50 km from the center). The trip to the city generally takes 45–60 minutes by road.
steps: After collecting your luggage, go to the official taxi or tuk-tuk counter in the arrivals hall.
Arrange a ride to 'Art Center Night Market' or 'Hospital Street (17000), Siem Reap'.
Confirm the drop-off point near the riverside entrance of the night market.
Keep the market's map location or Plus Code (9V24+W2F) handy to show the driver.

modes.title: Walking
modes.desc: Suitable for visitors staying near the town center.
steps: From Pub Street or the Old Market area, head south toward the Siem Reap River.
Cross the river and continue to Hospital Street (Street 17000).
The market entrance is along the riverside promenade — about 10–15 minutes on foot.

modes.title: Tuk Tuk
modes.desc: A common and flexible way to get around Siem Reap.
steps: Ask your hotel or a street tuk-tuk driver for a ride to 'Art Center Night Market'.
Show the driver the map location or Plus Code 9V24+W2F if needed.
Most trips from the town center take about 5–15 minutes depending on traffic.

modes.title: Bicycle
modes.desc: Good for short-distance movement around town.
steps: Rent a bicycle from your guesthouse or a local shop.
Follow the riverside road south toward Hospital Street.
Park your bike at the edge of the market area; always use a lock.

modes.title: Car / Taxi
steps: Book a taxi or use a ride arranged by your hotel.
Set the destination as 'Art Center Night Market, Hospital Street'.
Ask to be dropped near the main riverside entrance.

items.q: Where is Siem Reap Art Center Night Market located?
items.a: Siem Reap Art Center Night Market is located at 9V24+W2F, 17000 Hospital St, Krong Siem Reap, Siem Reap Province, Cambodia.

items.q: What time does Siem Reap Art Center Night Market open?
items.a: Usually from 16:00 to 23:00, Monday to Saturday. Hours may change.

items.q: Is Siem Reap Art Center free to visit?
items.a: Yes, Siem Reap Art Center Night Market is a public market space and generally does not require a general admission ticket.
Visitors of different ages can experience the evening market atmosphere.
Visitors may find local handicrafts, souvenirs and cultural products.

items.q: How do I get to Siem Reap Art Center Night Market from Pub Street or the Old Market?
items.a: Walk south toward the Siem Reap River, cross it and continue to Hospital Street (Street 17000); the walk takes about 10–15 minutes, or about 5–15 minutes by tuk-tuk.

items.q: What is the phone number of Siem Reap Art Center Night Market?
items.a: The publicly listed phone number is +855 63 963 331.

items.q: Where do the ratings and reviews on this page come from?
items.a: The 4.2 rating and 6,092 reviews shown on this page are synced from Google Maps user reviews, last synchronised October 2026. Copyright belongs to the original authors and Google Maps; use the 'View all reviews on Google Maps' link for the full list.

items.q: What is the weather like, and which season is best for an evening visit?
items.a: The year divides into a cool dry season from November to February (21–31 °C, the most comfortable evenings), a hot dry season from March to May (26–36 °C), and the monsoon from June to October, when short heavy showers are common and September to October is wettest. Late November to February is the best window overall; June to October is quieter but wetter. The live forecast at the top of this page includes the market's opening hours.

items.q: Does the market close when it rains?
items.a: Evening markets in Siem Reap normally keep trading through rain, and the stall canopies give some shelter. Showers in the monsoon season often pass within an hour. Paving becomes slippery, so grippy shoes are safer than smooth soles.

items.q: Are there restrooms, parking and ATMs nearby?
items.a: Restrooms inside the market quarter are limited, so the washrooms of nearby cafés, restaurants and shops are the usual option. There is no large dedicated car park; vehicles use the surrounding streets, which fill up from about 18:00. ATMs and banks are concentrated in the town centre, and cash in small notes is the most practical way to pay at the stalls.

items.q: Is the market accessible for visitors with reduced mobility?
items.a: The market is at street level and the main lanes are wide enough for a wheelchair or walking frame, but kerbs, cables and parked motorbikes need care, and narrow aisles are easier with a companion. Arriving between 17:00 and 19:00, before the aisles fill up, makes the visit considerably easier.

items.q: What should visitors avoid doing at the market?
items.a: Do not buy ivory, tortoiseshell, animal bone or objects sold as antiques or temple artefacts. Ask vendors before photographing them or their stall, and accept a refusal. Dress modestly at the temples within walking distance, avoid leaving plastic waste in the lanes, and settle a bargained price before an item is wrapped.

seasonal.title: Seasonal Visiting Strategy
seasonal.subtitle: Weather, water level and crowd patterns read together — based on the 1991–2020 thirty-year climate normal for Siem Reap Province.
seasonal.intro: Cambodia's year is organised by the monsoon, and the monsoon decides what an evening at the market feels like: how hot it is at 18:00, whether the paving is wet, and how many people are in the lanes. The table below turns that rhythm into practical choices.

seasons.name: Cool dry season
seasons.rain: Very little; the driest stretch of the year
seasons.comfort: The most comfortable evenings — lower humidity, light breeze
seasons.crowds: Peak travel season: busiest lanes and the fullest hotels
seasons.advice: Book accommodation ahead, bring a light layer for late evenings, and treat this as the best window for photography and for slow browsing.

seasons.name: Hot dry season
seasons.rain: Rare, though the first storms of the year can break in late April or May
seasons.comfort: Hot and humid; evenings stay warm after sunset
seasons.crowds: Quieter than the peak season, except around Khmer New Year in mid-April
seasons.advice: Visit after sunset rather than in the afternoon heat, carry water, and expect the town to be extremely busy during the New Year holidays.

seasons.name: Early monsoon
seasons.rain: Short, heavy afternoon or evening showers on many days
seasons.comfort: Humid, but the showers cool the evening down
seasons.crowds: Low season — the easiest time to move around and talk to makers
seasons.advice: Start later and keep an umbrella with you. Rain usually passes within an hour and the market keeps trading through it.

seasons.name: Peak monsoon
seasons.rain: The wettest months: long spells of rain and the highest river levels
seasons.comfort: Warm and humid; puddles and wet paving are normal
seasons.crowds: The quietest months of the year for the town
seasons.advice: Waterproof footwear helps more than an umbrella. Check that the streets around your accommodation drain well and allow extra travel time.

seasonal.bestLine: Late November to February gives the most comfortable evenings. If you prefer quiet lanes and lower prices, June to October is the trade-off: you accept rain and gain space. Khmer New Year in mid-April and the water festival in November are the two busiest periods in town, so plan transport and accommodation around them.
seasonal.waterTitle: Water level and the lake rhythm
seasonal.waterLine: Siem Reap province is shaped by the Tonle Sap, whose river reverses direction each year: during the monsoon the lake swells to several times its dry-season size, and from around November the flow turns back toward the Mekong and the lake drains. That flood pulse is why the regional calendar — planting, fishing and the boat-racing festival — sits where it does. In the town centre it shows up as higher river levels and a faster current from roughly August to November.
seasonal.note: Figures are long-term averages for Siem Reap Province describing typical conditions rather than a specific day. The market's opening hours and stall numbers do not change with the season.

audiences.title: Visit Plans by Traveller Type
audiences.intro: The same market works very differently depending on who is walking through it. The three plans below match route, pace and timing to how you travel.

plans.name: Families with children
plans.summary: Children enjoy the market most while it is still early and bright: fewer crowds, more room, and food stalls just starting the evening. Keep the visit short and finish before tiredness sets in.
plans.pace: Slow, with a seated break in the middle
stops: Enter from the Hospital Street side while the lanes are still quiet
Walk one loop of the craft stalls and let the children choose a single souvenir
Eat at the food rows before the peak crowd arrives
Finish with a drink at the quieter end, then leave before 20:30
plans.bring: Water, wet wipes, a light layer against mosquitoes after sunset and cash in small notes. A stroller works on the main lanes but is awkward in the narrow aisles.

plans.name: Photography & nature
plans.summary: The best light arrives just before sunset and again in the first hour after the lamps come on. Look beyond the market as well: the river and the temple grounds nearby are the natural subjects of the same evening.
plans.bestTime: 17:15 – 20:30 (golden hour, then blue hour with the lamps on)
plans.pace: Flexible: a slow first loop, then a second pass for detail shots
stops: Start on the riverside promenade for the pre-sunset light
Reach the market lanes as the lamps are switched on
Shoot the craft stalls from the aisle, never from inside a stall
Return to the entrance for a wide shot of the illuminated frontage
plans.bring: A fast lens for the evening light, a small tripod only where it does not block the walkway and a cloth for humid conditions. Always ask before photographing people or their work.

plans.name: Low mobility & step-free visit
plans.summary: A step-free visit is possible with some planning: the market sits at street level and the main lanes are wide enough for a wheelchair or walking frame, though kerbs, cables and parked motorbikes need care.
plans.pace: Short, with frequent stops and a planned exit
stops: Ask the driver to stop at the roadside entrance rather than across the street
Follow the widest perimeter lane instead of the central aisles
Use a food stall with seating and a clear approach for a rest
Leave by the same entrance you came in, while the lanes are still passable
plans.bring: A companion if possible, a folding walking stick and the market's phone number in case you need assistance on arrival.

visitPlans.title: Recommended Routes: Half Day & Full Day
visitPlans.intro: The market comes alive in the late afternoon, so both routes are built backwards from dusk: use the daylight for the town and finish where the evening trade begins.

halfDay.label: Half day
halfDay.summary: A compact route for a first visit: one craft stop, the town centre on foot and the market at its liveliest moment.

steps.title: Craft or market stop in the centre
steps.desc: Begin with a daytime look at the old market quarter or a craft workshop, where you can see how the goods sold in the evening are actually made.

steps.title: Walk the river and the temple grounds
steps.desc: Follow the riverside promenade north. It is the easiest way to understand how the centre is laid out, and the light is at its best at this hour.

steps.title: Coffee or a cold drink
steps.desc: Take a break before the evening rush. Restaurants in the centre start serving early and are calm at this point in the day.

steps.title: Arrive at Siem Reap Art Center Night Market
steps.desc: Enter from the Hospital Street side. Walk one full loop first, note what you want to buy, then go back for it.

steps.title: Eat at the market food rows
steps.desc: Choose a stall that is busy with local customers; turnover is the simplest sign of fresh food.

steps.title: Last purchases and exit
steps.desc: Buy what you shortlisted, then leave while the streets are still easy to cross. Tuk-tuks wait near the main entrance.

halfDay.note: Distances inside the centre are short: the market, the old market and the riverside are all within about 15 minutes on foot. Carry cash in small notes.

fullDay.label: Full day
fullDay.summary: For visitors who want the region's context before the market: a measured day with a proper break in the afternoon heat, ending at the evening market.

steps.title: Angkor Archaeological Park (optional, ticketed)
steps.desc: The region's best-known site lies a short drive north of town and needs its own ticket and several hours. With one day available, choose two or three temples rather than trying to see everything.

steps.title: Lunch and rest
steps.desc: Return to town for a late lunch and a proper break out of the heat. The early afternoon is the hottest part of the day and the market is still closed.

steps.title: Museum or craft workshop
steps.desc: A museum or a working workshop supplies the historical and technical background to the carving, silk and lacquerware you will see later at the stalls.

steps.title: Riverside walk and temple stop
steps.desc: Walk the promenade between the old market quarter and the northern bridges, with a short stop at a Buddhist temple in the centre.

steps.title: Siem Reap Art Center Night Market
steps.desc: Arrive as the stalls finish setting up. Walk the craft rows first and the food rows afterwards.

steps.title: Dinner at the market
steps.desc: Eat on site among the food stalls. Vegetarian and mild options exist, but ask: not every stall advertises them.

steps.title: Evening stroll, then back
steps.desc: Walk the illuminated lanes once more and use the exit closest to your transport. Stalls begin packing up towards 23:00.

fullDay.note: This plan assumes a full day in town. Angkor Archaeological Park is a separate, ticketed site with its own visitor rules, including dress requirements at the temples; treat it as its own half or full day rather than an add-on.

visitPlans.ticketNote: Both routes are self-guided and free of charge: the market itself has no general admission ticket. Costs arise only for optional items such as temple tickets, museum entry, meals, transport and purchases.

science.title: Understanding the Market
science.intro: A night market is an economy, a craft workshop and a piece of town planning at the same time. These short notes explain what is actually going on behind the stalls.

items.title: How the stalls are run
items.desc: Most stalls are small family businesses rather than branches of a chain. Stock is often produced within the province, and the same family may trade at several markets during the week, which is why prices can differ between stalls for goods that look identical.

items.title: The evening economy
items.desc: In Siem Reap the market employs far more people than the stallholders alone: drivers, cooks, cleaners, loaders and the workshops that supply the goods. An evening market concentrates that trade into a few walkable streets.

items.title: Why craft matters here
items.desc: The carving, weaving and lacquerwork sold in the centre descend from the artistic traditions of the Angkor period, kept alive by workshops across the province. Buying directly at a stall keeps more of the value with the maker.

items.title: Reading the motifs
items.desc: Many designs repeat motifs from temple reliefs: apsara dancers, lotus flowers, naga serpents and scenes from the churning of the ocean. Recognising them turns shopping into a short lesson in Khmer iconography.

items.title: The monsoon sets the calendar
items.desc: The regional year runs on the flood pulse of the Tonle Sap rather than on the calendar month. Rice, fish and travel all follow it, and the market's busiest evenings shift with the tourist and festival seasons that grew around it.

items.title: Night markets and food safety
items.desc: Food stalls with high turnover and visible cooking are the safest bet for visitors. Freshly cooked hot dishes carry lower risk than food that has been standing, and bottled or boiled water is the usual choice for drinking.

science.etiquetteIntro: The market is somebody's workplace and the surrounding streets are somebody's home. A few habits keep the visit pleasant for everyone.

etiquette.title: Take your waste back
etiquette.desc: Waste collection in the town centre struggles during the rainy season. Carry a small bag, reuse a bottle where you can, and never leave plastic in the lanes.

etiquette.title: Ask before photographing people
etiquette.desc: Photograph the goods freely, but ask vendors before photographing them or their stall, and accept a refusal without pressing the point. Do not use flash inside temples.

etiquette.title: Bargain politely, once
etiquette.desc: Gentle negotiation is normal in a market, but settle the price before an item is wrapped and pay the amount you agreed. Walking away after agreeing is not part of the custom.

etiquette.title: Dress for the temples
etiquette.desc: Several temples stand within walking distance. Cover shoulders and knees, remove shoes where indicated, and keep voices low when people are praying.

etiquette.title: Avoid wildlife and antique products
etiquette.desc: Do not buy ivory, tortoiseshell, animal bone, feathers or objects sold as antiques or temple artefacts. That trade is illegal, harms wildlife and cannot be exported lawfully.

etiquette.title: Respect the working day
etiquette.desc: Stalls are small and often run by one person. Do not block an aisle to take photographs, do not rearrange a display without asking, and move on when a vendor is serving other customers.

science.note: This page is written as non-commercial information: it names no business, accepts no sponsorship and takes no commission from any purchase made by readers.

compare.title: Art Center Night Market vs Other Siem Reap Night Markets
compare.intro: Siem Reap has several evening markets. They sit close together but serve different needs — knowing the difference helps you choose the right one.

items.name: Art Center Night Market
items.where: Hospital St (Street 17000), south of the river
items.known: Craft and souvenir rows, food stalls, open until 23:00
items.best: Buying handicrafts and a relaxed evening walk

items.name: Made in Cambodia Market
items.known: Curated local-maker stalls with live music
items.best: Quality gifts, an easy walk from Pub Street

items.name: Angkor Night Market
items.known: One of the original night markets, general souvenirs
items.best: A first taste of Siem Reap nightlife

compare.note: Opening hours and stall lists change. This page covers the Art Center Night Market and is not affiliated with the other markets.
